hints.title: Sequential Function Pipeline Execution
hints.text: A series of mathematical functions must be evaluated in right-to-left order, feeding the output of each function as input to the next. How can an array of functions be collapsed into a single composed function?

hints.title: Right-to-Left Reduction Invariant
hints.text: Function composition evaluates the rightmost function first and folds the result through successive functions toward the leftmost index.

hints.title: ReduceRight Composition Procedure
hints.text: Return a function accepting input x. Within it, call reduceRight on the functions array starting with accumulator x, updating accumulator with the result of calling each function.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: number of functions in composition array
complexity.notes: Linear pipeline execution from right to left using reduceRight.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Evaluating from left-to-right violates mathematical function composition f(g(x)), producing wrong results when operations are non-commutative.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Iterative reduction requires O(N) evaluation time and O(1) auxiliary memory beyond the returned closure.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Understanding reduceRight semantics; handling empty function array by returning the identity function x.
